paper_summary: Yazici (Acta Physica Polonica A 2016) develops syntactic foams from a rigid two-part polyurethane casting resin (Smooth-On Task 3) toughened with 10 wt% silicone rubber (MoldStar30) and filled with 10, 30 or 50 wt% 3M A20/1000 glass bubbles (0.2 g/cm3, 105 um), cast by hand mixing into wax molds. Quasi-static compression (Instron, 1 mm/min) shows density and yield strength decreasing with GB content while the plateau region extends; split Hopkinson pressure bar tests (about 2800 1/s) show type B (30 wt% GB) foam has roughly eight times higher strength than under quasi-static loading.

extraction_notes: Unit conversions: densities kg/m3 / 1000 -> g/cm3; 'Elongation [%]' in Table II interpreted as compressive strain at end of test (fraction); 'Comp. yield strength' mapped to strength_mpa. Quasi-static strain rate 0.00098 1/s is derived by the extractor from 1 mm/min crosshead speed on a 17 mm high specimen (not stated explicitly). GB contents are weight percentages ('30% GBs by weight'); volume fractions are not given and were not computed. Cure temperature 23 C assumed as room-temperature curing (resin datasheet values at 23 C). High-strain-rate (SHPB, ~2800 1/s) stress-strain curves for matrix and type B are only shown in Fig. 3b; the paper states type B strength is about eight times higher than quasi-static but gives no numerical value, so those properties are left null. The polyurea row is a literature comparison material (not a hollow-particle composite) included as a secondary record per rule 8; it may be filtered out downstream. Type C density (376 kg/m3) being higher than type B (252 kg/m3) is as printed in the paper.
